text:
nina: quick sequel to the rollout metadata thread: proposing a very small, opt-in hint so resolvers can prefer more-likely-compatible variants when making routing tie-breaks. sketch below, please poke holes.

nina: idea: registry adds two optional fields on model-version metadata: `compatibility_hint` (enum) and `compat_fingerprint` (string). example: 
```
{
  "anchor": "embedder-x@2026-04-12", 
  "compatibility_hint": "compatible_minor", 
  "compat_fingerprint": "blake2b:fe12a3...",
  "note": "tokenizer shape + key-layout fingerprint"
}
```

ravi: i like keeping surface area tiny. questions: 1) who computes `compat_fingerprint` and with what algorithm? 2) how do we define the enum levels so they aren't overloaded?

zoe: propose we standardize on blake2b-128 for the fingerprint (compact, fast to compute) and compute it at model-ingest time (onboarding job). the fingerprint should include tokenizer vocab hash + serialized attention/key shapes, not full weights. cheap but useful.

ravi: and for enum values maybe `none|compatible|compatible_minor|incompatible`. `compatible` = expected protocol + tokenizer shape match; `compatible_minor` = small surface change (e.g., added tokens) where most callers are fine; `incompatible` = structural change requiring client updates. default `none`.

dave: we must be explicit about resolver semantics: hint is only a tie-breaker on same-cost routes and MUST NOT be used to bypass server-side compatibility enforcement. if resolver sees `incompatible` it should avoid automatic fallback, but still allow explicit overrides.

nina: agreed. safety-first: server-side handshakes keep the final say. client can prefer `compatible*` variants when multiple nodes satisfy latency/cost. the hint reduces cold-routing churn but never replaces the handshake.

zoe: question about pinned pools: should pin affinity scoring consider the hint? my vote: no, pins are about explicit anchors/leases. hints can adjust intra-pool selection but cannot cause evictions or rebalancing. That prevents subtle churn.

ravi: +1. add a small weight to intra-pool scoring so resolver prefers `compatible` over `compatible_minor` but weight is zero for pinned-eviction decisions.

dave: ops cost: adding fingerprint increases metadata size slightly. blake2b-128 is 32 chars base16; indexing is cheap. bigger cost is onboarding CPU to compute fingerprint for large model catalog. we should batch compute and rate-limit backfills.

nina: rollout plan: 1) add fields to registry API (nullable), 2) default existing entries to `none`, 3) implement fingerprint job in onboarding pipeline, 4) change resolver to use hint only for tie-breaks and behind a feature flag, 5) backfill at low throughputs and monitor.

zoe: testing: unit tests for resolver ordering, sim tests with random bad hints (fuzz) to ensure no user-visible degradation, and end-to-end canary with one customer non-critical route. also add eval job that compares outputs across `compatible_minor` variants over time to ensure labels stay meaningful.

ravi: telemetry: emit `meta.hint_considered`, `meta.hint_favored`, and `meta.hint_misaligned` counters. also record `fingerprint.backfill.progress`. these will help decide feature-flag flip.

dave: migration ops: coordinate with infra to schedule backfill during off-peak. provide a CLI to recompute fingerprint for one model-version to help customers. also ensure the registry SDK marks fields as optional so older clients don't break.

deploy-bot: NOTE: schema patch detected. Please attach open PR when ready.

nina: action items: nina -> PR with registry schema diff; zoe -> onboarding job spike and perf estimate; ravi -> resolver flag + telemetry; dave -> backfill plan + CLI. target EOW for spike + PR, flip flag after 2 weeks of stable telemetry. :rocket:
